9.4.5. qnav.gps.zones

9.4.5.1. zones.py

summary:

Handles the representation and method connected with zones/areas. This module contains a family of classes used for representing and querying zones. This has been designed for reuse, with various child area-polygon classes and their associated group handlers.

author:

Michael Wright - mjwright@liverpool.ac.uk

version:

1.0.0 - First implementation of this module.

class qnav.gps.zones.Polygon(lat_points: ndarray, lon_points: ndarray, priority: int = 0)[source]

Represents a simple latitude-longitude closed polygon. Can be used for defining custom 2D zones on the globe.

is_point_inside(lat_point: float, lon_point: float) → bool[source]

Determines if a given position is inside the polygon. Given the latitude and longitude coordinates of a single point in decimal degrees, this function will return True if the point is inside the polygon.

Parameters:

  • lat_point (float) – The latitude coordinate of the point of interest.

  • lon_point (float) – The longitude coordinate of the point of interest.

Returns:

Returns True if given point is inside the polygon.

Return type:

bool

is_points_inside(lat_points: ndarray, lon_points: ndarray) → ndarray[source]

Determines if a series of positions are inside the polygon. Given the latitude and longitude coordinates of a multiple points in decimal degrees, this function will return True for each point that is inside the polygon.

Parameters:

  • lat_points (float) – The latitude coordinates of the points of interest.

  • lon_points (float) – The longitude coordinates of the points of interest.

Returns:

Returns True for each given point inside the polygon.

Return type:

bool

property lat_points: ndarray

Returns the list of latitude coordinate points of the polygon. This property returns a copy, preventing accidental editing.

Returns:

The latitude coordinate points of the polygon.

Return type:

np.ndarray

property lon_points: ndarray

Returns the list of longitude coordinate points of the polygon. This property returns a copy, preventing accidental editing.

Returns:

The longitude coordinate points of the polygon.

Return type:

np.ndarray

property priority: int

Returns the priority (or layer) of the polygon. This is used for determining the outcome when multiple polygons overlapping one another are involved. When this occurs the highest priority polygon is used.

Returns:

The priority (or layer) of the polygon.

Return type:

int

class qnav.gps.zones.FlaggedPolygon(lat_points: ndarray, lon_points: ndarray, is_active_area: bool, priority: int = 0)[source]

Represents a latitude-longitude closed polygon with binary active flag. These polygons are used for determining “active” and “inactive” areas. For example, areas where specific sensors, such as where GPS or quantum sensors can and cannot be used.

property is_active_area: bool

Returns True if the polygon is active area. This can be used to determine if points which are found inside the polygon are to be considered inside an active area.

Returns:

Whether the polygon is an active area.

Return type:

bool

class qnav.gps.zones.FlaggedPolygonGroup(polygons: List[FlaggedPolygon], is_active_by_default: bool = True)[source]

A handler for a group of flagged polygons. Allows the querying of multiple polygons, in priority order, with a default flag.

get_point_flag(lat_point: float, lon_point: float) → bool[source]

Returns the boolean flag for given point. Searches through given polygons in priority order and returns the flag for the highest priority polygon that the point is inside of. If the point is not in any polygons, the default flag will be used.

Parameters:

  • lat_point (float) – The latitude coordinate of the point of interest.

  • lon_point (float) – The longitude coordinate of the point of interest.

Returns:

Boolean flag of the highest priority polygon the point is inside of (or the default flag for the group).

Return type:

bool

property polygons: List[FlaggedPolygon]

Returns list of flagged polygons used by group.

Returns:

list of flagged polygons used by group

Return type:

List[FlaggedPolygon]

property num_polygons: int

Returns the number of polygons covered by the group.

Returns:

The number of polygons covered by the group.

Return type:

int

get_point_flags(lat_points: ndarray, lon_points: ndarray) → ndarray[source]

Returns the boolean flags for multiple given points. Searches through given polygons in priority order and returns the flags of the highest priority polygons that each of the point is inside of. For points that do not fall inside nay polygon’s the default flag is used.

Parameters:

  • lat_points (np.ndarray) – The latitude coordinates of the points of interest.

  • lon_points (np.ndarray) – The longitude coordinates of the points of interest.

Returns:

Boolean flags of the highest priority polygon each point is inside of (or the default flag for the group).

Return type:

np.ndarray

qnav.gps.zones.is_inside_polygon(x_point: float, y_point: float, polygon_x: ndarray, polygon_y: ndarray) → bool[source]

Determines if a given position is inside given the polygon. Tests by generating horizontal lines and assessing the number of polygon lines that are crossed. Using this count, a point can be determine to be inside the closed polygon or not.

Parameters:

  • x_point (float) – The x coordinate of the point of interest.

  • y_point (float) – The y coordinate of the point of interest.

  • polygon_x (np.ndarray) – The x-coordinates of the polygon. Assumed to be closed.

  • polygon_y (np.ndarray) – The y-coordinates of the polygon. Assumed to be closed.

Returns:

Returns True if the given position is inside the polygon.

Return type:

bool

qnav.gps.zones.is_inside_polygon_vec(x_points: ndarray, y_points: ndarray, polygon_x: ndarray, polygon_y: ndarray) → ndarray[source]

Determines if a given position is inside given the polygon. Tests by generating horizontal lines and assessing the number of polygon lines that are crossed. Using this count, points can be determine to be inside the closed polygon or not.

Parameters:

  • x_points (float) – The x coordinates of the point of interest.

  • y_points (float) – The y coordinates of the point of interest.

  • polygon_x (np.ndarray) – The x-coordinates of the polygon. Assumed to be closed.

  • polygon_y (np.ndarray) – The y-coordinates of the polygon. Assumed to be closed.

Returns:

Returns True if the given position is inside the polygon.

Return type:

bool
